dedupe_keys.name: carec corridor performance measurement and monitoring cpmm border crossing and corridor time and cost indicators

description: The CAREC Corridor Performance Measurement and Monitoring programme measures how quickly and cheaply goods move along the six CAREC transport corridors across Central Asia, the Caucasus, Mongolia, western China and Pakistan. It is based on samples of actual commercial cross-border shipments collected with national partner associations, and has run for more than a decade. Coverage: the CAREC countries (Azerbaijan, the People's Republic of China, Georgia, Kazakhstan, the Kyrgyz Republic, Mongolia, Pakistan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan among them); the Annual Report 2024, published in July 2026, gives trade facilitation indicators (TFIs) for road, rail and multimodal shipments, including time and cost to clear border-crossing points, corridor speed with and without delay, activities at border-crossing points, the costliest rail border points, change of gauge, perishables and TIR transit, and country tables for 2022 to 2024. Format and access: yearly PDF reports on the CAREC Institute site, free; the method and statistical derivation of each indicator are set out in the report's appendices. Licence: CC BY 3.0 IGO, as stated in the 2024 report. Caveats: indicators are derived from shipment samples, so coverage varies by corridor and year; the report gives summary statistics, and the shipment-level data were not found for download. Simulation uses: border delay and corridor speed parameters for freight network flow, capacity planning and resilience models of Eurasian trade corridors. Related records: none yet in the catalogue for Central Asian freight corridors.
